name: Kellstrom BioWatch Lab Coat
description:
Kellstrom Biological Systems is a Tier 4 corponation subsidiary focused on geneware development and pharmaceutical synthesis. Their BioWatch Lab Coat is standard-issue for wet-lab personnel working in contact with biological agents, but it's also sold as a standalone item to independent researchers, biotech startups, and anyone who works in environments where contamination is a genuine concern. The coat is a mid-thigh length in a bright white polymer-cotton blend that resists most common chemical and biological surface contamination. It's treated with a hydrophobic coating that causes most liquids to bead and run off rather than soak in. The cuffs are snug and adjustable. The pockets are sealed with press-closure flaps.

Outside of lab environments, the BioWatch has developed an unexpected secondary life. Geneware modification clinics — particularly the unlicensed ones operating in the Tier 2-3 boundary zones — use them because they suggest legitimacy. Some artists have adopted the clean white as a canvas. A few people just like the look of a good lab coat and wear it over street clothes, a choice that reads somewhere between scientific and eccentric depending on the neighborhood.
functionality: Chemical and biological surface contamination resistance. Hydrophobic outer treatment. Cuff seals rated for splash protection.
what_it_says: You work with things that could hurt you, or you want people to think you do.
worn_by: artists using the white as canvas
story_hooks: A BioWatch coat recovered from an unlicensed geneware clinic has contamination on the cuffs that doesn't match anything in the clinic's official inventory — someone was working on something else.
A Kellstrom researcher went missing wearing one; the hydrophobic coating preserved a partial handprint on the sleeve that nobody has been able to match.
An artist who paints in their BioWatch has been documenting what they witness at a Tier 2 geneware clinic on the interior lining — a running record hidden under the white exterior.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp, clinical silhouette that reads institutional and authoritative. Mid-thigh length with a slightly boxy cut that drapes cleanly over the body. The bright white creates a stark, almost luminous presence in urban settings, making the wearer appear either competent or conspicuously out of place depending on context.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with fitted, adjustable cuffs at the wrists. Designed for layering over street clothes or protective gear without restriction. The cut allows freedom of movement for lab work — arms sit slightly away from the body rather than hugging.
physical_description.primary_material: Polymer-cotton blend with hydrophobic treatment. The fabric has a slight sheen that catches light, distinguishing it from natural cotton. Resists chemical and biological surface contamination.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and slightly stiff when new, developing a soft broken-in quality with wear. The hydrophobic coating gives it a subtle waxy feel that repels moisture visibly. Seams are reinforced and appear structurally overbuilt compared to casual wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Bright pharmaceutical white as primary color. No patterns. Occasionally shows subtle discoloration or faint staining from use that persists despite the hydrophobic coating — a badge of actual lab work or aesthetic affectation.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit buttons down the front placket (usually white or chrome depending on manufacturing batch). Press-closure flaps on all pocket openings to create sealed compartments. Wrist cuffs have adjustable snap closures.
distinctive_features: Sealed pocket flaps with press closures for contamination control
Adjustable, snug cuffs designed for glove compatibility
Hydrophobic coating visible as bead-pattern water resistance
Reinforced seams and structurally robust construction
Kellstrom Biological Systems logo embroidered subtly on left chest pocket
Multiple internal and external pockets of varying depths
Slightly stiff fabric drape that emphasizes clinical aesthetic
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 boundary. Legitimizes the wearer within medical/research spaces (Tier 4 institution standard-issue), but affordable and accessible enough for independent researchers and geneware modification clinic operators. When worn casually, signals either genuine expertise or performative authority.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by licensed biotech workers, independent researchers, unlicensed geneware modification clinic staff seeking legitimacy, underground biomodding enthusiasts, and street-level artists using the blank canvas. In the GLMZ, it's become a cultural marker of someone engaged with biology — whether legally or not.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; develops subtle discoloration and faint chemical stains with heavy use. Well-maintained lab versions show minimal wear. Street-worn versions may have reinforced patches, marker art, or deliberately distressed sections. The hydrophobic coating eventually degrades, making older coats absorb stains despite their original purpose.
